## Introduction

`uRbano` is designed to support urban ecological workflows that combine spatial data acquisition, gridded summaries of urban structure, and alternative field sampling designs. This vignette walks through a complete example in which we build a circular study extent around Minneapolis, generate a hexagonal grid, quantify buildings and roads within each grid cell, and compare multiple candidate sampling schemes.

The workflow has five main parts:

1. define the study area,
2. prepare building and road layers,
3. create the sampling grid,
4. calculate grid-level urban metrics, and
5. generate and visualize sampling schemes.

Because some functions rely on external spatial data downloads, you may prefer to set the download-heavy chunks to `eval = FALSE` for package checks, or replace them with bundled example objects in a production vignette.

## Installation

`uRbano` is currently available on GitHub. We recommend installing it using the `pak` package, which provides fast and reliable dependency resolution.

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#install.packages("pak")
library("pak")
library("ggplot2")
library("sf")
pak::pkg_install("MSP-LTER/uRbano", ask = FALSE)

```

## 1. Create a city-centered study extent

We start by creating a circular buffer around a city chosen by text input and the radius covering the study area in meters:
Saint Paul, MN with a 30 km radius:


```{r, cache=TRUE, echo=FALSE}

get_city_rad <- function(city, radius, selection = NULL) {
  cty <- subset(maps::world.cities, maps::world.cities$name == city)

  if (nrow(cty) == 0) {
    stop("No cities found matching the criteria")
  }

  if (nrow(cty) > 1) {
    cat("Multiple cities found:\n")
    for (i in 1:nrow(cty)) {
      cat(sprintf("%d: %s, %s (Pop: %s)\n", i, cty$name[i], cty$country.etc[i],
                  format(cty$pop[i], big.mark = ",")))
    }

    # Only prompt if no selection was supplied
    if (is.null(selection)) {
      selection <- as.numeric(readline(prompt = "Please select a city by number: "))
    }

    if (is.na(selection) || selection < 1 || selection > nrow(cty)) {
      stop("Invalid selection")
    }

    cty <- cty[selection, ]
  }

  cty_coords <- sf::st_as_sf(cty, coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = 4326)
  cty_crc <- sf::st_buffer(cty_coords, radius)

  return(cty_crc)
}

```


```{r, eval=FALSE}
rad<-uRbano::get_city_rad("Saint Paul", 30000)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
rad<-get_city_rad("Saint Paul", 30000, selection=2)
```
Select number 2

## 2. Extract OSM network and Microsoft building footprints for the city radius

We extract roads from OpenStreetMap within the study area. The larger the radius around the city, the more time it may take to download the road length data.


```{r, cache=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results=FALSE}
rds<-uRbano::extract_osm_rds(rad)
```
```{r}
ggplot()+geom_sf(data=rds)

```

Then we get building footprints.
Since parts of Wisconsin enter the radius on the other side of the St. Croix river, we can specify two regions:

```{r, cache=TRUE}
blds<-uRbano::get_bldgs("Minnesota", "Wisconsin")
```
buildings from both regions are bound together as a simple features collection, each feature is a single building polygon
```{r}
ggplot()+ geom_sf(data=blds[999,])+theme_void()
```

Crop the buildings to the extent of your city
Also clean up invalid geometries that could halt the calculation of area later on
(Spherical geometry gets turned off and back on to restore previous setting)
```{r, cache=TRUE}
bldgs<- uRbano::fix_n_trim_bldgs(blds,rad)

```

Now we want to get the units of our spatial objects in meters for calculating area
selecting the NAD method will look up the North America Datum EPSG coordinate reference system based on the location of your city. In this case it is UTM Zone 15N, 26915
```{r}
rad_m<-uRbano::transform_to_meters(rad, "NAD")
rds_m<-sf::st_transform(rds, crs=sf::st_crs(rad_m))
bldgs_m<-sf::st_transform(bldgs, crs=sf::st_crs(rad_m))

rad_m
```

## 3. Create uniform hex grid across the study radius
we are choosing hexagons of 1km across

```{r}
SP_grid<-uRbano::radius_hex_grid(rad_m, 1000)
ggplot()+geom_sf(data=SP_grid)
```

## 4. Calculate road length and building area per hexagon
We summarize two features of urban structure calculate inside each hexagon of the grid:
- total building area per grid cell
- total road length per grid cell
this can take a little while depending on the size of your radius and number of grids...


```{r, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
SP_grid$bldg_ars <- uRbano::calculate_blds_by_grid(SP_grid, bldgs_m)
SP_grid$rd_len <- uRbano::calculate_rds_by_grid(SP_grid, rds_m)
```

The resulting values can be combined into a "built density" index for plotting
These variables can later be used as predictors, descriptors of the urban environment, or stratification variables for sampling.

To create a coarse urbanization gradient, we classify building area and road length per hex into quantiles. For readability, this vignette uses the name `dens_index`.


```{r}
SP_grid$bldg_index <- cut(
  SP_grid$bldg_ars,
  breaks = quantile(
    SP_grid$bldg_ars,
    probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  include.lowest = TRUE,
  labels = FALSE
)

SP_grid$rd_index <- cut(
  SP_grid$rd_len,
  breaks = quantile(
    SP_grid$rd_len,
    probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  include.lowest = TRUE,
  labels = FALSE
)


SP_grid$dens_index<-replace(SP_grid$rd_index, is.na(SP_grid$rd_index), 0) + replace(SP_grid$bldg_index, is.na(SP_grid$bldg_index), 0)

ggplot() +
    geom_sf(
      data = SP_grid,
      aes(fill = dens_index),
      color = "white",
      linewidth = 0.1
    )
```

## 5. Run different sampling methods on the grid

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

samples<-uRbano::create_sampling_functions(SP_grid, "dens_index")
samples
```

```{r}
ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data=SP_grid)+
  geom_sf(data=samples$simple_random, fill="hotpink")+
  geom_sf(data=samples$cardinal_transects, fill="purple")+
  geom_sf(data = samples$density_stratified, fill="skyblue")+
  geom_sf(data=samples$concentric_rings, fill="orange")+
  geom_sf(data=samples$random_transect, fill="green")
  

```
